title: Equivalent Fractions
course_context: Undergraduate demonstration lesson; all content is supplied through configuration.

objectives.title: Explain equivalent fractions
objectives.description: Construct equivalent fractions and justify why multiplying numerator and denominator by the same nonzero factor preserves the value.
success_criteria: Uses the same factor on numerator and denominator
Explains unchanged value using a fresh example
objectives.diagnostic_prompt: Create an equivalent fraction and justify the unchanged value.

misconceptions.description: Changing only the numerator generally changes the fraction’s value.
misconceptions.counterexample: One half of a pizza is not three halves; the number of equal parts must change along with the number counted.

required_task.title: Reflection
required_task.description: Reflect on what you can explain or do now.
required_task.submission_prompt: What can you explain or do now that you could not before?

study_resources.title: Fractions and Equivalent Fractions
study_resources.description: An open textbook explanation of fractions and equal partitions.
study_resources.focus: Compare selected and total pieces, and use diagrams to explain equivalent fractions.

diagnostic_quiz.question: In the fraction 2/5, what does the denominator represent?
options: The number of equal parts in the whole
diagnostic_quiz.explanation: The denominator counts equal parts in the whole.
diagnostic_quiz.hint: Think about how a whole is divided into equal parts.
distractor_misconceptions: Misapplies denominator meaning: The number of parts selected
Misapplies denominator meaning: A multiplication sign
Misapplies denominator meaning: Always the larger number

diagnostic_quiz.question: Why do 1/2 and 2/4 represent the same amount?
options: The second picture splits the same selected amount into smaller equal parts
All fractions have the same value
diagnostic_quiz.explanation: Both fractions select the same proportion of the whole.
diagnostic_quiz.hint: Compare the selected amount, rather than counting pieces alone.
distractor_misconceptions: Misapplies equivalence: Their numerators are equal
Misapplies equivalence: All fractions have the same value
Misapplies equivalence: Their denominators are equal

diagnostic_quiz.question: Which fraction is equivalent to 2/3?
diagnostic_quiz.explanation: Multiplying numerator and denominator by two gives 4/6 with unchanged value.
diagnostic_quiz.hint: A valid transformation preserves the relationship between selected parts and total parts.

diagnostic_quiz.question: A student changes 2/3 to 4/3 and says the value is unchanged. What is wrong?
options: Every numerator can be doubled independently
The numerator changed without the denominator changing by the same factor
diagnostic_quiz.explanation: The same factor must be applied to numerator and denominator to preserve value.
diagnostic_quiz.hint: Check what happened to each part of the fraction.
distractor_misconceptions: Misapplies same-factor misconception: No change is needed
Misapplies same-factor misconception: Every numerator can be doubled independently
Misapplies same-factor misconception: Fractions cannot be transformed

diagnostic_quiz.question: A diagram splits every piece of a 3/5 whole into three smaller equal pieces. Which describes the selected amount?
options: 9/15, because both selected and total pieces triple
3/15, because selected pieces do not split
diagnostic_quiz.explanation: Multiplying numerator and denominator by the same factor of three preserves the proportion.
diagnostic_quiz.hint: Follow the change in both selected pieces and total pieces.
distractor_misconceptions: Misapplies transfer to a partition diagram: 9/5, because only selected pieces matter
Misapplies transfer to a partition diagram: 3/15, because selected pieces do not split
Misapplies transfer to a partition diagram: 15/9, because numerator and denominator swap

learning_assets.explanation: Track selected parts (numerator) and total equal parts (denominator). Apply the same factor to both to preserve the proportion.
learning_assets.worked_example: A rectangle with one of two equal parts selected can be split into four parts with two selected, so 1/2 = 2/4.
learning_assets.analogy: Changing the size of the tiles in a picture changes their count without changing the selected area. The analogy assumes equal-sized pieces of the same whole.
learning_assets.counterexample: Doubling the number of selected pieces without splitting the whole changes the proportion; 1/2 and 2/2 are not equal.

topic_introduction: Equivalent fractions name the same proportion of a whole using different equal-sized parts. Multiplying numerator and denominator by the same nonzero factor changes the partition, not the selected proportion.
approved_material: The denominator is the total number of equal parts in the whole; the numerator is the number selected. Equivalent fractions name the same proportion. Multiplying numerator and denominator by the same nonzero number preserves the fraction value because the selected count and total count change in the same ratio. Changing just one generally changes the value. A partition diagram makes both counts visible.
introductory_example: A half of a rectangle can be shown as two of four equal pieces: 1/2 = 2/4.
prerequisite_knowledge: Basic reading and arithmetic; no prior subject knowledge is required.
